A.title: Who Really Drew Africa's Borders? (It Wasn't Berlin) #shorts
A.description: In 1884, fourteen delegations met in Berlin to decide Africa's future. Not one of them was African. But Berlin didn't actually draw the borders. Full story on the channel. #history #africa #maps #shorts
A.pinned_comment: Did you learn in school that Berlin drew Africa's borders? 👇
A.first_line: In the winter of 1884, a group of men gathered around a table in Berlin.
A.last_line: ...in dozens of separate deals between European powers, one border at a time.

B.title: Why Are Africa's Borders So Straight? #shorts
B.description: Some borders follow rivers and old kingdoms. Others were drawn with a ruler, in an office far away from the desert they cut through. Full story on the channel. #geography #africa #maps #shorts
B.pinned_comment: Which country has the weirdest border you know? 👇
B.first_line: Why do so many of them still look like someone used a ruler?
B.last_line: Sometimes those lines were simply lazy, and sometimes they were spectacularly wrong.

C.title: Germany Traded an Island for a Road to a Waterfall #shorts
C.description: In 1890, Germany got a thin strip of Africa so it could sail to the east coast. One problem: Victoria Falls. Full story on the channel. #history #namibia #maps #shorts
C.pinned_comment: Would you have spotted the waterfall problem? 😅👇
C.first_line: In 1890, Germany made a deal with Britain.
C.last_line: Today, the strip is still there, a strange little handle on the map of Namibia.
